what_this_is: The model-and-representation pairs the uncertainty work runs, and the ONLY place they are written down. Both pipelines answer the same uncertainty questions on the same pairs, so a table can put QM9 beside logD, Caco-2 and hERG row for row. A second list anywhere means the two halves stop being comparable, which is what happened between 2026-08-28 and 2026-08-29.
the_decision: The author, 2026-08-28: 'The same thing that happens on QM9 happens on the others. Pick 5 or so interesting/well-performing model/rep pairs and run them through the circus of uncertainty on all datasets.' The membership was left open pending the roster screen ('leave that as a flexible decision pending more uncertainty results in the rerun plan') and was settled by the author on 2026-08-29: four models, three representations, and the variational network on ChemBERTa alone.
why_it_had_to_be_written_down: The screen's cut was applied to the laboratory job generator and to nothing else. QM9 has no uncertainty run of its own -- its uncertainty rows fall out of the main grid -- so every model that emits one was cross-fitted on every representation, 11 models by 6 representations against the laboratory's 10 pairs. The two halves could not be compared pair for pair, which is exactly what the decision asked for.

models.why: first on both measures on all six representations in the screen, and the cheapest
second on four representations of six; kept because it is the noise-robust model the study highlights
the only non-tree model that shows anything, and what it shows depends on the representation
the one Bayesian network worth running, and badly overconfident, which is itself the finding

decomposition._what_this_is: The models whose uncertainty is split into a measurement-error half and a model-doubt half, and reported as such. A SUBSET of `models` above -- a model cannot have its split reported if it is not run at all. Every other model on the uncertainty list still writes a total uncertainty; it simply does not have a split reported.
decomposition._the_decision: The ordinary Gaussian process, on the re-measurement of 2026-08-31 (3,000 real QM9 molecules, PDV, out of fold on scaffold groups, the LABEL STANDARDISED as the pipeline standardises it): as the injected noise grows, its aleatoric term grows 17.2-fold while its epistemic term grows 1.5-fold, and it keeps its clean accuracy at 0.85. Its two terms are the same SIZE as each other (0.000135 and 0.000235 on clean labels), so both are real quantities and one rising while the other holds still is a genuine separation. It is the only model on the uncertainty list that both fits and separates.
decomposition._every_other_model_was_measured_too: Same run, same molecules. The variational network FITS QM9 perfectly well -- R2 0.84, not the -0.04 recorded before the label was standardised -- and fails the test on its merits: both of its terms rise together, 4.6-fold and 4.1-fold. The random forest fails the same way, 5.7 and 5.3, because one bootstrap causes both. NGBoost has no epistemic term to test. So the list is one model not because the others were untested, but because they were tested. RERUN_PLAN.md 5.5i carries the full table.
decomposition._why_ngboost_is_not_here: It was, for one day. NGBoost over three seeds was reported at 9.1-fold against 0.7-fold, which reads as a pass. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-30 on 3,000 real QM9 molecules, PDV, out of fold on scaffold groups, at four settings of the two parameters NGBoost's seed actually reaches: the epistemic term is 150 to 3,581 times SMALLER than the aleatoric term, and it RISES with the noise level (1.6 to 2.7-fold) rather than holding still. The 0.7 and the 1.9 my own run gave at the same setting are both noise on a quantity that has no stable sign. NGBoost's seed feeds only `minibatch_frac` and `col_sample`, both pinned at 1.0, so the three fits are the same fit. Subsampling makes the term 24x bigger and it is still dust, and accuracy does not move (0.840 to 0.842). So NGBoost has NO epistemic term at any setting -- which is what a single distributional fit having nothing to disagree with looks like -- and `ngboost_ensemble_seeds` is back to 1. Its ALEATORIC term is real, is the second best measured at 9.1-fold against the Gaussian process's 17.2, and NGBoost stays on the uncertainty list above for it. See RERUN_PLAN.md 2.30.
decomposition._which_question_this_answers: The POPULATION one: does the measurement-error half grow with the noise actually injected, while the model half holds still. It does NOT answer the per-molecule one -- does the measurement-error half point at the individual molecules whose labels were corrupted. The Gaussian process cannot answer that by construction: its measurement-error term is one number for the whole fit, so it is the same for every molecule and correlates with per-molecule noise at exactly zero however good the model is. Do not report a per-molecule detection statistic from these two.
decomposition._why_the_others_are_not_here: The quantile forest is the only model on the uncertainty list whose two halves both vary per molecule, and both of its halves track the injected corruption at +0.84 and +0.81 -- one signal reported twice rather than a separation (RERUN_PLAN.md 2.25). The variational network reports its ALEATORIC half as one number for the whole fit, so that half is the same for every molecule; the split is defined for it as a population statement and it has not been measured to pass the level-response test. Its coverage is also badly wrong on the roster screen -- the truth falls inside one standard deviation 23% to 45% of the time against a target of 68%, on the three settled representations -- so its interval is not yet trustworthy either.
decomposition._a_number_NOT_used_here: An earlier version of this entry said the variational network fails to FIT on QM9, quoting an out-of-fold R2 of -0.03. That number came from scripts/decomposition_controls.py, whose _standardise scales the features and never touches the LABEL, and a network is not scale-invariant while a tree is. With the label standardised the same networks reach R2 +0.68 to +0.73 (RERUN_PLAN.md 2.31). The roster screen that chose these four models is NOT affected -- it went through the production pipeline, which standardises, and its errors are on a unit scale (0.26 to 0.61 mean absolute error against a label spread of 1.0). The choice of models stands on the screen; only the discarded reason was wrong.
decomposition._what_this_costs: Nothing. The Gaussian process already decomposes -- it needed no change at any point -- and the split is read off a fit that is being made anyway.

model_representations._why: A model that is only worth running on some of the three. The list is the CANONICAL representation names. A model absent from here runs on all three.

notes.what_this_does_NOT_restrict: The main QM9 grid still trains every model on every representation -- the accuracy results, the retention curves and the variance decomposition all need the full grid, and none of them reads an uncertainty column. This file decides only which pairs get the out-of-fold uncertainty pass and write per-molecule uncertainty rows.
notes.cost: The out-of-fold pass costs `--oof-folds` extra fits on top of each training run, so restricting it is a saving on QM9 rather than an expense.
notes.the_decomposition_models: heteroscedastic_gp, dnn_bnn_full_variational_hetero and mlp_bnn_full_variational_hetero are NOT in this list, because they are not in the laboratory run either. They are the only models that report a data-noise term that varies per molecule (RERUN_PLAN.md 5.5e, 5.5f), so the aleatoric/epistemic split cannot be measured per molecule on the pairs listed here. Raised with the author rather than resolved by this file.
